extracted.intended_audience: readers, visitors, and students of medieval cathedral sculpture and iconography
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance for interpreting and evaluating thirteenth-century cathedral sculpture and iconography, especially the west front/porches of Amiens Cathedral; includes typologies, theological emphases, and aesthetic criteria. Intended to help a reader decode subjects, styles, and moral messages in the carvings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sculptures as signs/guides to thought
rubrics_metrics.description: They were never intended to serve as more than signs, or guides to thought.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Read the sculptures as didactic devices rather than full narrative paintings; follow the guidance quietly and allow them to prompt imaginative pictures in your mind rather than expect exhaustive representation or literal realism.

rubrics_metrics.name: Christ portrayed as Incarnate Word and present Lord
rubrics_metrics.description: Throughout the Sermon on this Amiens Mount, Christ never appears... as the Crucified, nor as the Dead: but as the Incarnate Word--as the present Friend--as the Prince of Peace on Earth,--and as the Everlasting King in Heaven.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Interpret Christ-figures as teaching present duty and the living example rather than emphasizing past suffering; prioritize scenes and gestures that instruct viewers on how to live here and now.

rubrics_metrics.name: Emphasis on present duty and inner disposition
rubrics_metrics.description: "This do, and thou shalt live; nay... This be and thou shalt live: to show Mercy is nothing--thy soul must be full of mercy; to be pure in act is nothing--thou shalt be pure in heart also."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When decoding scenes, look for moral imperatives aimed at inner state as much as outward action; carvings stress being and character, not merely ritual or external performance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Martyrdom and the building's foundation as communal memory
rubrics_metrics.description: Every stone of this building is cemented with his blood, and there is no furrow of its pillars that was not ploughed by his pain.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Understand and evaluate depictions of martyrs and persecuted apostles as anchors of communal identity and moral teaching; the presence of martyrs grounds the cathedral's message in sacrifice and remembrance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Iconography reveals doctrinal emphasis (presence/absence of doctrines)
rubrics_metrics.description: There is no word in thirteenth-century Theology of the pardon (in our modern sense) of sins; and there is none of the Purgatory of them... the language of every graven stone... was absolutely and alone, this teaching of Moses from Sinai in the beginning, and of St. John from Patmos in the end.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use the subject-matter and emphases of the carvings to infer the theological positions they express (e.g., stern judgment, lack of explicit purgatorial imagery); do not superimpose later doctrinal developments onto earlier iconography.

rubrics_metrics.name: Typology of Madonnas for dating/style assessment
rubrics_metrics.description: Three sorts of Madonnas: (1) Madonna Dolorosa; the Byzantine type, the noblest and earliest; (2) Madone Reine, the Frank and Norman one; crowned, calm, full of power and gentleness; (3) Madone Nourrice, the Raphaelesque late and decadent type.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Classify Virgin figures by these types to assess period and stylistic lineage; compare examples side-by-side (with caution—comparative drawings can flatter or vulgarize forms, as Viollet le Duc is accused of doing).

rubrics_metrics.name: Months and zodiac as allegory of providence and blessing
rubrics_metrics.description: The quatrefoils represent the pleasant order of the guarded and hallowed year--the zodiacal signs above, and labours of the months below... all the seasons and signs are regarded as alike blessing and providentially kind.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Read representations of labours and zodiacal signs allegorically as affirmations of providence; note unusual or instructive deviations (e.g., May depicted as a man listening to birds, Libra shown as a female holding scales).

rubrics_metrics.name: Evaluate technical and aesthetic qualities (modeling, drapery, expression, action)
rubrics_metrics.description: Several [figures] peculiarly refined and far-wrought... the lion especially good-tempered--and the 'reaping' one of the most beautiful figures... the incapability of the sculptor to give strong action or passion... Virgo above, holding a flower, her drapery very modern and confused for thirteenth-century work.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess individual reliefs on craftsmanship: refinement of carving, quality of modeling (e.g., shells, flowers), naturalism of drapery, ability to render action and passion; use specific exemplars cited (reaping, lion, Virgo) as benchmarks.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sequence of subjects less important than unified message
rubrics_metrics.description: I have no doubt of finding out in time the real sequence of these subjects: but it is of little import,--this group of quatrefoils being of less interest than the rest.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not overvalue exact narrative sequencing of minor panels when the primary interest is the overall theological and moral message; concentrate on thematic unity rather than reconstructing a precise order unless sequence materially alters meaning.

rubrics_metrics.name: Local/provincial subjects as pastoral teaching to community
rubrics_metrics.description: The other saints in this porch are all in like manner provincial, and, as it were, personal friends of the Amienois; and under them, the quatrefoils represent the pleasant order of the guarded and hallowed year.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Interpret the inclusion of local saints, labours, and customs as deliberate pastoral pedagogy aimed at the cathedral's contemporary community; situate iconography within local history and civic identity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of comparative illustration and photography to study details
rubrics_metrics.description: In Mr. Kaltenbacher's photographs, as I have arranged them, the bas-reliefs may be studied nearly as well as in the porch itself... I directed their setting so that the entire succession of the quatrefoils might be included in eighteen plates.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use carefully made photographs or comparative plates to examine sequence, detail, and stylistic features when in-person study is impractical; follow authorial plate references to relate text descriptions to images.

rubrics_metrics.name: Read figures in relation to scriptural references and prophetic panels
rubrics_metrics.description: The quatrefoils underneath the great statues run as follows: [lists of biblical scenes under each statue]... join the beautiful C and D of Amos.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Decode individual panels by mapping them to specific biblical episodes or prophetic figures; connect adjoining prophet panels to understand allusions and theological continuities across the façade.
